assessment.intent: Give busy small business owners a practical, non-legal guide to basic website accessibility checks, anchored to the W3C's first-review checklist.
assessment.specificity: Strong. Concrete checks for keyboard focus, contrast and 200% zoom, alt text decisions, form labels and error messages, captions and transcripts, and a six-row first-pass worksheet. No invented metrics or client stories.
assessment.evidence: Three appropriate W3C sources (first checks, forms tutorial, audio/video guide). Internal links to the author's web design page and good-design article are natural and not self-congratulatory.
assessment.voice: Calm, conversational, Canadian spelling, answer-first H2s. No banned phrases, no corporate padding, no smug contrasts. Recommendations are framed as recommendations.
assessment.usefulAsset: Yes. The worksheet table and the short FAQ add real value beyond the headings and make the piece usable as a self-review tool.
